1.title: Azure Networking
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Azure Networking. It covers the exam area Describe Azure architecture and services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Describe virtual networking, including the purpose of Azure virtual networks, subnets, peering, Azure D N S, Azure V P N (virtual private network) Gateway, and Express Route. Define public and private endpoints. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Azure virtual networks
1.text: Azure virtual networks. An Azure virtual network (V net) is your private, isolated network in Azure. Resources placed in it (V Ms, app services with network integration, and more) can talk to each other, to the internet and to on-premises networks. Address space. The private I P range of the V net (for example ten point zero.zero point zero or sixteen). Subnet. A segment of the V net's address space; you place resources in subnets. Region. A V net lives in one region and one subscription. Isolation. V nets are isolated from each other by default. A V net provides. Communication between Azure resources (privately). Communication with the internet (outbound by default; inbound only if you allow it). Communication with on-premises (through V P N Gateway or Express Route). Filtering and routing of traffic (network security groups, route tables).

1.title: Azure virtual networks, continued
1.text: Azure virtual networks. The figure shows this: A virtual network with two subnets, peering, V P N Gateway and Express Route.

1.title: Azure virtual networks, continued
1.text: Azure virtual networks. Subnets let you segment a network, for example one subnet for web servers and another for databases, and apply different security rules to each. Exam tip: A network security group filters traffic to and from resources in a subnet with allow and deny rules. The skills list does not name N S Gs, but V M questions often mention them.

1.title: Virtual network peering
1.text: Virtual network peering. V net peering connects two virtual networks so resources in each can communicate privately, with low latency, over the Microsoft backbone network, not the internet. Works across regions too (global V net peering). Resources use private I P addresses to reach each other. Peering is non-transitive: if A peers with B and B peers with C, A and C are not connected unless you peer them as well. Exam tip: "Connect two Azure virtual networks privately" to V net peering.

1.title: Azure DNS
1.text: Azure D N S. Azure D N S is a hosting service for D N S domains that provides name resolution using Microsoft's global network. You manage your D N S records with the same credentials, billing and tools as other Azure services. Use it to host your public domain (for example fabrikam dot example ) and map names to I P addresses. Private D N S zones resolve names inside your virtual networks. Azure D N S does not sell or register domain names; it hosts the records.

1.title: Connecting to on-premises: VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute
1.text: Connecting to on-premises: V P N Gateway and Express Route. Connection. Azure V P N Gateway: Encrypted tunnel over the public internet. Azure Express Route: Private, dedicated connection through a connectivity provider. Goes over the internet? Azure V P N Gateway: Yes (encrypted). Azure Express Route: No. Speed and latency. Azure V P N Gateway: Depends on the internet. Azure Express Route: Higher, more predictable, lower latency. Reliability. Azure V P N Gateway: Good. Azure Express Route: Higher (provider connection, redundancy).

1.title: Connecting to on-premises: VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute, continued
1.text: Connecting to on-premises: V P N Gateway and Express Route. Cost and setup. Azure V P N Gateway: Lower, quick. Azure Express Route: Higher, needs a provider. Typical use. Azure V P N Gateway: Small to medium sites, remote users, backup path. Azure Express Route: Large data volumes, critical or regulated workloads.

1.title: Connecting to on-premises: VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute, continued
1.text: Connecting to on-premises: V P N Gateway and Express Route. V P N Gateway connection types. Site-to-site: connects an on-premises network to a V net. Point-to-site: connects a single client computer to a V net. VNet-to-VNet: connects two V nets. Exam tip: V P N equals encrypted over the internet. Express Route equals private line, not the internet. If the question says "does not go over the public internet", "dedicated" or "higher reliability", pick Express Route.

1.title: Public and private endpoints
1.text: Public and private endpoints. Address. Public endpoint: A public I P address reachable from the internet. Private endpoint: A private I P address from your V net. Traffic. Public endpoint: Over the internet (can be restricted). Private endpoint: Stays on the Microsoft backbone, inside your network. Use. Public endpoint: Services meant to be reached publicly. Private endpoint: Reach a pass service (storage, sequel) privately. A private endpoint is a network interface that connects you privately and securely to a service powered by Azure Private Link. It brings the service into your V net using a private I P. Exam tip: "Access an Azure storage account only from the virtual network, without exposing it to the internet" to private endpoint.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors has two virtual networks in different regions and wants resources in each to talk privately over the Microsoft backbone. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: V net peering. V net peering connects virtual networks privately, including across regions.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company needs a connection to Azure that does not travel over the public internet and offers predictable performance. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Express Route. Express Route is a private connection through a provider and does not use the public internet. V P N Gateway is encrypted but uses the internet.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An administrator wants to connect an on-premises office network to Azure quickly with an encrypted tunnel over the internet. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: V P N Gateway (site-to-site). A site-to-site V P N uses an encrypted tunnel over the internet.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. What does a private endpoint give a storage account? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A private I P address from the virtual network. A private endpoint places a network interface with a private I P in the V net for the service.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What is a subnet? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A segment of a virtual network's address space. Subnets divide the address space so resources can be grouped and secured separately.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which service hosts D N S records and provides name resolution on Microsoft's network? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure D N S. Azure D N S hosts D N S domains and resolves names. It does not register domain names.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is a virtual network? Answer: A private, isolated network in Azure. Question two. What does V net peering do? Answer: Connects two virtual networks so they communicate privately over the Microsoft backbone. Question three. V P N Gateway or Express Route: which avoids the public internet? Answer: Express Route.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the three V P N Gateway connection types. Answer: Site-to-site, point-to-site and VNet-to-VNet. Question five. Which kind of endpoint uses a private I P address from your V net? Answer: A private endpoint. Question six. Does Azure D N S register domain names? Answer: No. It hosts D N S records for domains you own.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. V net: private isolated network in one region; address space split into subnets. Subnet: segment of the V net; apply separate rules. Peering: connects V nets privately over the Microsoft backbone, also across regions. Azure D N S: hosts D N S records and name resolution; private zones inside V nets. V P N Gateway: encrypted over the internet; site-to-site, point-to-site, VNet-to-VNet. Express Route: private dedicated connection through a provider, not the internet. Endpoints: public equals public I P; private equals private I P in your V net (Private Link). In the next module, we continue the course.
